question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to introduce globally named MCP servers, and if so, what host-authorized broker/allowlist and sharing policy governs stdio commands, environments, and cross-agent reuse?
rationale: This is a durable security and ownership contract for a new core lifecycle feature. A mechanical patch cannot safely choose whether global sharing is supported, how a host authorizes it, or which command and environment capabilities are legitimate.

options.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP resources
options.body: Accept only host-approved command brokers or allowlisted MCP resources and require explicit authorization before any global reuse.

options.title: Namespace MCP resources per Claw
options.body: Avoid cross-agent reuse by deriving isolated resource identities and treating every shared declaration as unsupported for the first experimental release.

options.title: Defer MCP lifecycle ownership
options.body: Keep Claw MCP declarations out of the experimental lifecycle until the RFC establishes the process and sharing contract.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP resources
recommendation.body: Accept only host-approved command brokers or allowlisted MCP resources and require explicit authorization before any global reuse.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to this PR and their prior review identifies the source-config, persistence, and lifecycle invariants the permanent policy must preserve.
